title: What Really Happens During Dijkstra's Algorithm
production_path_basis: The flagship showcase cycle requires explanations that remain complete without narration or music.
assumed_knowledge: graphs contain nodes and weighted edges
a path cost is the sum of its edge weights
a priority queue can return a smallest key
central_message: Dijkstra repeatedly settles the smallest tentative distance and relaxes its outgoing edges.
takeaway: With non-negative weights, the smallest unsettled distance cannot be improved later; predecessors recover the route.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
scientific_depth: introductory single-source shortest paths, relaxation, predecessor reconstruction, and negative-edge boundary
visual_direction: dark execution dashboard with stable graph geometry and semantic state colors
pacing: one complete relaxation cycle followed by accelerated verified snapshots
constraints: visible frontier means best current entry per unsettled node
do not claim validity for negative edge weights
success_criteria: all displayed values match the generated trace
accepted and rejected relaxations are visually distinct
the final path and cost are correct
the negative-edge counterexample is numerically valid
graph geometry remains fixed across snapshots
